editorial.description: An extended underpainting tutorial contrasts making a living with making an image, hides garish early colors beneath later work, questions the performance of mature gallery art and uses stopping movement to reconsider an old survival strategy.
editorial.summary: An extended underpainting tutorial contrasts making a living with making an image, hides garish early colors beneath later work, questions the performance of mature gallery art and uses stopping movement to reconsider an old survival strategy. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.

Garish colors no one may see

connections.note: The route uses a studio art process to organize autobiographical reflection; metaphor is part of the exercise and is not medical advice.
The video treats revision, imperfection and emotional attention as more important than copying a polished Choe image.

publication_restrictions.rule: Do not present mental-health, addiction or trauma metaphors as diagnosis or treatment; preserve them as the artist’s framing.

source_notes: Focus and chapter beats were reviewed against this route transcript.
The transcript cannot fully encode tools, color changes, gestures or the developing canvas; use the source video for technique replication.
Claims about personal history remain attributed to Choe.
editorial.speaker_policy: David Choe is the public route-level presenter. Off-camera voices remain unnamed without validated diarization.
